newsitem.title: FRANCE: France invites, recognises Serbia opponents.
newsitem.headline: France invites, recognises Serbia opponents.

text.p: France, condemning police repression of pro-democracy protesters in Belgrade, invited the three leaders of Serbia's opposition coalition to visit Paris as soon as possible in a significant policy switch.

"This invitation amounts to recognition by the French government of the leaders of the Zadejno opposition coalition, which through the past weeks has proved its political maturity," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said in a statement.
"I have decided to invite the three leaders of the democratic opposition in Belgrade, Mr Zoran Djindjic, Vuk Draskovic and Mrs Vesna Pesic to come to Paris as soon as possible," de Charette said.

He said France condemned "with the utmost firmesss" Sunday's police violence against peaceful demonstrators who have been protesting for weeks at alleged election fraud by the hardline socialist government of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

"(France) solemnly warns the Serbian authorities against a slide into violence which can only lead to a disastrous outcome for their country," de Charette said. The explicit recognition of the opposition was a departure from Paris's previously cautious stance.
He said Belgrade must abide by the conclusions of an OSCE mission led by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez and accept the opposition victory in last year's disputed municipal elections.
